name: Remitly Global, Inc.

profile.description: Remitly is a leading digital financial services provider for immigrants and their families, enabling cross-border remittances through its mobile app. The platform facilitates money transfers from 17 sending countries to over 170 receiving countries across 5,100+ corridors, processing $22.1B in quarterly send volume (Q1 2026). Founded in 2011 by Matt Oppenheimer, who now serves as Chairman. Based in Seattle.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Remitly delivered record Q1 2026 revenue of $452.8M (+25% YoY), with active customers growing 20% to 9.6M and send volume surging 37% to $22.1B [1]. The company expanded from 17 sending to 170+ receiving countries across 5,100+ corridors and launched new products including card-based 'Send Now, Pay Later' and wallet offerings [1]. AI Deployment (2/2): Remitly's Q1 2026 profitability surge was driven by AI-powered efficiency — ML fraud detection reduced intervention rates by 25%+, an AI virtual support assistant resolves issues 4x faster (75% reduction in resolution time), and the company cited AI as comparable to the internet/mobile shift in transformative potential [2]. Adj EBITDA crossed $100M for the first time at 22% margin, partly driven by these AI efficiencies [1]. Market Share (1/2): Remitly is a leading digital remittance player in a fragmented $900B+ global market, competing against Wise, Western Union, and MoneyGram. Growing faster than most peers but not the category leader. Pipeline (1/2): Raised 2026 guidance to $1.96-1.975B revenue with Q2 guidance of $483-485M, plus expansion into broader financial services beyond core remittance [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Technology is the core business — substantial engineering investment in AI, ML fraud detection, and platform scalability positions Remitly above fintech industry average R&D intensity.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Remitly's mission to 'transform the lives of immigrants and their families by providing the most trusted financial services on the planet' is specific, service-oriented, inclusive, and connects the business to a genuine social purpose [3]. Founder Matt Oppenheimer built the company after witnessing remittance challenges firsthand in Kenya. The mission clearly shapes strategic decisions — expanding to 170+ countries, investing in accessibility, and emphasizing trust over price competition. Falls short of a 4 only because it hasn't been tested through multi-decade consistency. Community Impact (1/2): The business model itself serves underbanked immigrant populations by reducing remittance costs and increasing speed. Company ESG programs exist but specific charitable dollar amounts are not publicly quantified [3]. Employee Retention (1/2): Founder Oppenheimer led for 15 years before transitioning to Chairman in February 2026, demonstrating long-term commitment. Some Glassdoor reviews praise culture of openness, but others cite frequent pivots and cultural challenges [2]. Insider Buying (1/2): Oppenheimer's transition to Chairman (maintaining significant equity) and an institutional investor's $21M stock purchase following FY2025 earnings signal continued conviction in the long-term story [1].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Liquidity check passes: 4,490,000 avg vol x $23.75 = $106.6M >> $1M floor. Calculated mechanically for growth-stock metrics. D/E of 4% scores 1.0 (1x weight) — near debt-free balance sheet with $649M cash vs $39M debt [5]. ROE of 12.95% scores 0.86 (2x weight) — rapidly improving from loss-making years as profitability inflects [5]. Revenue Growth YoY of 25% (Q1 2026) scores 1.0 (1x) [1]. Revenue Growth 5yr CAGR of ~45% scores 1.0 (2x weight) — exceptional growth trajectory from ~$300M (2021) to ~$1.6B (2025) [1]. Forward P/E of 15.0 scores 1.0 (1x) — reasonable for a 25%+ revenue grower [5]. Profit Margin of 6.1% scores 0.31 (1x) — improving rapidly with Q1 2026 net income of $49M (+332% YoY) and adj EBITDA margin reaching 22% [1]. PEG excluded (null). Weighted sum = 1.0 + 1.73 + 1.0 + 2.0 + 1.0 + 0.31 = 7.04 / max 8 x 10 = 8.8, rounds to 9.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Remitly's core business is protected by formidable regulatory and network moats that AI cannot replicate — money transmission licenses across 17 sending countries, banking and payout partnerships in 170+ receiving countries, and compliance infrastructure for AML/KYC that requires years of regulatory relationship-building [2]. Converting stablecoins or AI-processed transfers to local fiat currency still requires the same physical-world payout infrastructure and regulatory approvals. While AI enhances competitors' ability to reduce transaction costs, Remitly's own AI deployment creates a defensive moat: fraud detection, intelligent routing, and automated support improve unit economics on every transaction [1]. The main risk vector is that a tech giant (Google, Apple) could leverage AI to enter remittances, but the regulatory barriers remain substantial. AI Opportunity (1/1): Remitly generates measurable AI-enhanced revenue — Q1 2026's adj EBITDA margin of 22% (first time crossing $100M) was explicitly driven by AI efficiencies in fraud detection and customer support automation [1]. The ML fraud system reduces intervention rates by 25%+ and the AI virtual assistant cuts resolution time by 75%, directly improving unit economics across $22.1B quarterly send volume [2].

infinite_game.summary: Remitly demonstrates genuine infinite game characteristics through its immigrant-focused mission, 15 years of consistent purpose-driven execution by founder Matt Oppenheimer, and willingness to invest through years of losses to build regulatory and network infrastructure. The February 2026 CEO transition to Sebastian Gunningham introduces uncertainty about whether the mission will remain central, but Oppenheimer's continued role as Chairman and the strong Q1 2026 results under new leadership provide early reassurance. Cultural challenges identified in Glassdoor reviews and the 'disruption' competitive framing are finite game elements in an otherwise infinite-leaning organization.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Remitly's mission to 'transform the lives of immigrants and their families' is a genuine Just Cause in Sinek's framework — it's service-oriented, inclusive, idealistic, and bigger than any single product [3]. Oppenheimer built the company after witnessing remittance challenges in Kenya, and every major strategic decision (expanding to 170+ countries, investing through years of losses, launching SNPL) traces back to this purpose. However, the cause hasn't survived a true crisis or multi-decade leadership test — the February 2026 CEO transition is its first real test of durability.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Remitly invested through 10+ years of operating losses to build its regulatory licenses, banking partnerships, and technology platform before achieving first GAAP profitability in FY2025 — a textbook example of choosing long-term capability over short-term earnings [1]. The $649M cash position was built through patient capital raising rather than premature profit optimization. However, Glassdoor reviews citing frequent strategic pivots and inconsistent annual plans temper the courage narrative with execution concerns [2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Mixed signals on organizational trust. Founder Oppenheimer led for 15 years, and the internal promotion culture (CFO, CTO roles filled from within) suggests some career development infrastructure [3]. However, Glassdoor reviews describe micromanagement, frequent layoffs, and cultural challenges including an 'aggressively masculine culture' in some teams [2]. The 3,200-employee organization appears to have pockets of high trust but systemic challenges as it scales rapidly.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Remitly has evolved from a single-corridor remittance app to a multi-product digital financial services platform — adding wallets, SNPL (Send Now, Pay Later), and expanding to 5,100+ corridors across 170 countries [1]. The company is using stablecoins on its balance sheet to minimize transfer costs, showing technological adaptation. However, the core business model (digital remittance facilitation) has not fundamentally changed since founding — these are incremental extensions, not transformative pivots.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Remitly competes against Wise, Western Union, and MoneyGram, but CEO commentary focuses on serving immigrants better and building trust rather than 'beating' specific competitors [3]. Oppenheimer's public statements emphasize 'expanding access' and 'building belief' rather than market share conquest. The competitive response has been to improve Remitly's own product — faster transfers, lower costs, better fraud protection — rather than attacking competitors' weaknesses.

investment_thesis: Remitly delivered a record Q1 2026 with revenue of $452.8M (+25% YoY), net income of $49M (+332%), and adj EBITDA crossing $100M for the first time at a 22% margin, driven by AI-powered operational efficiency [1]. Active customers grew 20% to 9.6M and send volume surged 37% to $22.1B. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to $1.96-1.975B revenue. At 15.0x forward P/E with near-zero debt (D/E 4%, $649M cash), Remitly offers exceptional growth-at-a-reasonable-price in a $900B+ global remittance market protected by formidable regulatory moats [5]. The profitability inflection from losses to 22% adj EBITDA margin demonstrates the operating leverage embedded in the platform as scale increases and AI-driven efficiencies compound.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on growth deceleration, competitive pressure, and leadership transition. Revenue growth slowed from 34% (FY2024) to 25% (Q1 2026), and Q2 guidance of $483-485M implies further deceleration to 17-18% — the market may re-rate the multiple downward as Remitly transitions from hypergrowth to sustained growth [1]. GAAP profit margin of 6.1% remains thin and could compress if Wise, Western Union Digital, or crypto-native competitors intensify pricing pressure on take rates [5]. The CEO transition from founder Oppenheimer to Sebastian Gunningham in February 2026 introduces execution risk at a critical scaling moment, despite encouraging early Q1 results. Glassdoor reviews citing frequent layoffs, micromanagement, and cultural challenges suggest organizational growing pains that could impair talent retention [2]. Trailing P/E of 43.6x (vs 15.0x forward) shows how dependent the valuation is on earnings projections materializing.
key_catalysts: Adj EBITDA margin expanding from 22% (Q1 2026) toward 25%+ as AI-driven efficiencies in fraud detection and customer support continue to compound across growing send volume [1]
Expansion beyond core remittance into broader digital financial services — SNPL, wallets, and new products increase addressable market and customer lifetime value [1]
Forward P/E of 15.0x for a 25% revenue grower with regulatory moats represents significant undervaluation vs fintech peers — re-rating to 20-25x forward would drive 33-67% upside [5]
key_risks: Revenue growth deceleration from 34% to 25% to 17-18% Q2 guidance risks multiple compression if the market re-rates RELY as a mature fintech rather than a hypergrowth story [1]

CEO transition from founder Matt Oppenheimer to Sebastian Gunningham introduces execution uncertainty — new CEOs at high-growth companies frequently reset expectations despite encouraging Q1 2026 results [2]
Competitive pricing pressure from Wise (lower fees), Western Union Digital (brand trust), and crypto-native solutions could compress take rates on the growing $22.1B quarterly send volume [2]
